learning_outcomes.text: Justifies project decisions based on the scientific and technological foundations of the specialty. Applies knowledge in basic subjects to design a project.
Prepares technical reports. Applies topographical techniques to field problems.

Completes an original exercise to be carried out individually and presents and defends it before a university panel, consisting of a project in the field of specific Industrial Engineering technologies of a professional nature in which the competencies acquired in the studies are synthesized and integrated.
Knows the basic legislation that applies to the project and knows where to find it.
Plans tasks to be carried out at each project stage using bar charts or other simple techniques.

Culminates the acquisition of competencies that characterize the degree in an integrating project. Integrates the knowledge and skills of a Mechanical Engineer with direct experience in the development of an original technical project.

Intervenes effectively and transmits relevant information, appropriate to the situation. Plans communication: generates ideas, seeks information, selects and organizes information, creates outlines, determines the type of audience, communication objectives,... Drafts documents with the correct format, content, structure, linguistic accuracy, appropriate register, and illustrates concepts correctly using conventions: formats, titles, footers, legends,... Their presentations are properly prepared, using strategies to present and deliver oral presentations (audiovisual aids, gaze, voice, gestures, time control,...).
Responds effectively to changes experienced during the course of studies.
Is able to overcome difficulties arising from work, both individually and in a group.
Defines the tasks that allow project objectives to be achieved. Establishes clear objectives for the project.
Foresees and allocates necessary time to complete planned actions.

Analyzes the work or professional environment of the field of study (environment). Designs academic and professional insertion itineraries (itineraries). Identifies their own learning process (learning). Deepens academic, work, or professional self-knowledge (self-knowledge).
Makes significant contributions or certain innovations. Transfers learning from classroom cases and exercises to real situations in other fields.

Gathers significant information needed to solve problems based on objective criteria. Presents different alternative solution options for the same problem and evaluates their possible risks and advantages.

Recognizes ethical and deontological concepts of the area of knowledge, demonstrates critical and dialogue capacity, and makes responsible use of the norms that affect them as a member of the university community. (Ethics)
Identifies main environmental problems. (Environment) Recognizes and reflects on social needs and problems and gets involved in improving the community. (Social responsibility as a citizen)

teaching_methods: Introductory activities: The general operation of the course will be presented, clearly specifying the basic program for developing the TFG.

Coordination and follow-up mechanisms for the final degree / master's project: As a general procedure, students must: choose a supervisor, register the project, submit it with the supervisor's approval, and defend it orally.

Selection/assignment of the final degree / master's project: There will be a group of project supervisors who will propose the areas of projects they can supervise. In some specific cases, the supervisor will also propose a specific topic. Students will choose up to 5 supervisors they wish to work with, in order of preference. The coordinator will assign the supervisor to each student according to specific criteria. Once the supervisor is assigned, students must define the TFG topic, always advised by the supervisor.
Elaboration of the final degree / master's project: The student will adequately develop, always guided and advised by their TFG supervisor, the specific project of their specialty.

Presentation and defense of the final degree / master's project: Submission of formal documentation: as described in the TFG's own regulations. This work must be accompanied by the supervisor's approval. Oral defense of the TFG: before the same panel that evaluated the formal documentation. Once the TFG is submitted, a rules exam will be conducted to verify that the submitted documentation is formally correct.

assessment_methods.method: Supervisor's approval and formal documentation review
Technical quality of the project (evaluated during defense, considering tutor's opinion)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on the technical quality of the project (75%) and the quality of the presentation and defense (25%). The submission of the work requires the supervisor's approval and a formal documentation review, which is essential. The panel will consider the supervisor's opinion on the work's development and quality. All information regarding this course is fully and exhaustively collected in its own TFG regulations. Mobile phones, tablets, and other electronic devices not expressly authorized must be switched off and out of sight during assessment activities.
